title: Guest account holding a directory role
summary: A guest account that was granted a directory role is used to read the directory and hand privileged access to another account.

steps.title: Starting assumption
steps.text: A guest account was given a directory role during a project and never removed. The attacker controls that guest account.

steps.title: Sign-in evaluated by Conditional Access
steps.text: The guest signs in through a browser and its role rights come along. Only guest-focused controls treat this account differently from a normal member.

gaps.text: Guest sign-ins are not restricted, so an external account can carry a privileged role.

fix.caTemplate: Restrict guest access with Conditional Access

steps.whenFixed: Blocked: guest access is restricted, so the external account cannot use its role.

steps.title: Directory read
steps.text: The attacker lists users, groups and roles to map the organization. This makes it easy to choose high-value targets.
steps.whenFixed: Guest directory access is restricted, so the account cannot enumerate other users.

steps.title: Another account promoted
steps.text: The attacker adds a second account to a privileged role to keep control if the guest is removed. This creates a standing back door.
steps.whenFixed: The role change is written to the audit log and surfaces for review.

outcome.prevented: Guest restrictions and directory limits stop the external account from reading or escalating.
outcome.notPrevented: The attacker maps the tenant and plants a second privileged account.
